subject: Observability partner triage: telemetry delta across Datadog & Grafana OTLP pipeline
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@datadog.com>, Marco Santini <marco@grafana.com>, ben.carter@redwood.inference, laura.bennett@redwood.inference, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference
Cc: OTLP Integrations <otlp-partners@acme-consulting.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Observability partner triage: telemetry delta across Datadog & Grafana OTLP pipeline

Hi Elena, Marco —

Thanks for taking this call yesterday. We surfaced a recurring issue where some inference-specific metrics (prefix token latency and kv-cache hit rate) are arriving in Grafana dashboards but are missing or aggressively sampled in Datadog for the same OTLP ingestion stream. The customer (Observify) sees inconsistent cost accounting across platforms and wants a clear triage path.

Quick context: Redwood’s agent emits OTLP v1.9 with a custom resource attribute (redwood.cluster) and a tokenized metric namespace (redwood.inference.*). We suspect an OTLP exporter sampling/aggregation mismatch between your ingestion layers and a schema mapping difference on Grafana’s side.

Ask: can each partner confirm the following by COB Monday EU time?
- A minimal repro (curl or small python snippet) that demonstrates the metric arriving/not arriving into your system
- Any ingestion-side sampling, deduping, or dimension limits that might drop high-cardinality attributes
- Recommended temporary workaround (e.g., prefix-based metric routing, dimension trimming) we can ship as a canary to the customer

I’ve attached our initial OTLP gap dump (otlp_gap_report.pdf) and a starter mutual action plan workbook. I’ll coordinate lab access and short-term retention increases for logs if needed.

Proposed owners: Datadog (Elena) — reproduce + ingestion logs; Grafana (Marco) — schema mapping + dashboard mapping; Redwood (Ben, Laura, Karthik) — repro harness and canary rollout.

Thanks —
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Partner Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena@datadog.com>

Cc: Marco Santini <marco@grafana.com>, OTLP Integrations <otlp-partners@acme-consulting.com>
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observability partner triage: telemetry delta across Datadog & Grafana OTLP pipeline

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the summary. We can reproduce a gap in our ingestion for a specific pattern: high-cardinality resource attributes combined with small batch sizes from the exporter appear to trigger our sampling heuristics on high-throughput agent flows.

Action items from Datadog side:
- We’ll run the provided repro harness (please point us at a short-lived test token) and capture ingestion logs (will attach once done).
- Temporary workaround: enable "preserve_high_cardinality_metrics" flag in our agent for this customer — this prevents early sampling but increases cost.
- Long-term: we want to propose a mapping rule that normalizes redwood.cluster to a lower-cardinality alias for indexing while preserving the raw attribute as metadata.

Attaching initial ingestion log excerpt and a quick note on the flag.

Cheers,
Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Field Engineering, Datadog
elena@datadog.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Observability partner triage: telemetry delta across Datadog & Grafana OTLP pipeline

Appreciate the quick response, Elena.

Ben here — to speed repro, I’ve dropped a tiny python harness into the shared Drive (link in the MAP). It emits three variations:
1) full resource attrs (high-cardinality)
2) trimmed attrs (cluster alias)
3) batched aggregator (larger batch windows)

I’ll wire a short-lived test token and run a canary to Observify’s staging tomorrow morning (EU). If we see Datadog sampling still, we’ll flip the preserve flag and measure delta on cost.

Notes: Karthik, Laura — please check if the agent’s default batch_size (currently 128 events) should be raised for the staging canary. That might reduce the sampling trigger.

Ben

Ben Carter

From: Marco Santini <marco@grafana.com>

Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 08:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observability partner triage: telemetry delta across Datadog & Grafana OTLP pipeline

Thanks team —

We looked through our ingestion schema; Grafana Cloud accepts the raw OTLP payload and does a conversion to our internal metric model. We do not sample in the ingestion tier for this payload shape, but our dashboarding indexer prunes labels exceeding 120 unique values per metric by default.

Workarounds we can offer:
- Create an explicit alias index for redwood.cluster (maps high-cardinality values into a tagset) so dashboards keep stable performance.
- Alternatively, we can add an ingest-time transform to prefix-strip unnecessary host-level tags if you prefer preserving cluster as metadata only.

I’ll attach a short transform example in the next message. For now: our ops suggestion is to run the canary with the cluster-alias approach. That gives the customer stable dashboards while Datadog preserves detailed raw events as metadata.

—Marco

--
Marco Santini

Thanks everyone — great alignment. Quick summary and next steps (owner in parens):
- Datadog will run the repro harness and share ingestion logs (Elena) — target: 2027-05-10 EOD UTC.
- Redwood will run a staging canary with cluster-alias and increased batch_size (Ben/Karthik) — target: 2027-05-11 09:00 UTC.
- Grafana will prepare an ingest-time alias transform and a dashboard mapping guide (Marco) — target: 2027-05-11 17:00 UTC.
- We’ll hold a short remediation sync 2027-05-12 08:00 UTC — calendar invite to follow.

I’ve updated the Mutual Action Plan (attached) with owners and acceptance criteria. Please add any risks to the Drive doc. If Datadog needs higher retention for the ingestion logs, Ben — I’ve approved a temporary bump for Observify.

Short note: this is a good candidate for a co-engineered field note (coauthored) that we can publish with partners once resolved — helps future customers.

Thanks —
Sofia
